rows.details: NLUD Justice for Children Research Fellowship

content_sections.heading: About NLUD
content_sections.text: National Law University Delhi (NLUD) runs the NLUD Chair on Justice for Children, which was established in collaboration with UNICEF. The Chair offers the NLUD Justice for Children Research Fellowship, which the notice calls a flagship programme for young graduates committed to research on access to justice for children in need of care and protection and children in conflict with the law. The fellowship aims to build a body of well-researched and accessible scholarship on child rights within the Indian criminal justice system.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: The notice names a Law Graduate (LL.B. or B.A.LL.B.) as the qualification for the Research Fellow (Delhi) post. The employment type is contractual and full-time. Updated knowledge of substantive and procedural child rights law, including POCSO and JJ Act Experience showing demonstrable work in child rights research Efficiency in legal writing Proficiency in English Proficiency in the use of MS Word and PowerPoint An LLM or an equivalent Master's degree in Law, Social Science, or other related fields Proficiency in the use of MS Excel, AI tools, and graphic design tools Proficiency in social media outreach Candidates should check the official notification for any further eligibility details.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: The Research Fellow receives a stipend of INR 50,000/- per month. The engagement is contractual and full-time, for 12 months starting December 15, 2026, at National Law University Delhi. The notice mentions no allowances.

content_sections.heading: NLUD RESEARCH FELLOW (DELHI) Job Description
content_sections.text: The research fellows are expected to contribute scholarship to two publications. Legal developments, including policy changes, amendments to the law, and judicial decisions. Opinion pieces, including interviews with child rights experts and actors (judges, lawyers, police officers, activists, academics, etc.). Notes from the field that highlight the experiences, successes and challenges of child rights litigation in India, based on real-time data collected through the NLUD Justice for Children Litigation Fellowship. A series of white papers based on analyses of data collected by the national and state-level Juvenile Justice Committees.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for NLUD RESEARCH FELLOW (DELHI)
content_sections.text: Open the application form at careers.nludelhi.ac.in, the link given in the notice. Submit the application there by 30 November 2026. Do not send any application material by post or email. Queries can be sent to [email protected] . The notice names no documents to be attached.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted, and they advance to the interview stage of the selection process. The notice gives no interview date, venue or shortlisting criteria.
